SETTING Medical Centre

PATIENT You are a 40-year-old long-term smoker (over 20 years) with a history of epilepsy
since childhood. You have been trying to quit smoking by yourself with no other
aids but have been unsuccessful, Your friend quit after taking Zyban (bupropion),
an anti-smoking medication, and you have come to the doctor to ask for a

prescription.
TASK * Tell the doctor you have been a heavy smoker since you were 18 years old and

have tried to quit many times using only your willpower. Ask for a prescription of
Zyban.

e Express dismay when the doctor explains that Zyban |s not suitable for
epileptics.

Insist that your friend had no problem with the drug and you are prepared to
take the risk.

¢ Remind the doctor that you have tried to quit many times and feebyou cannot do
it without the drug.

¢ Listen to the alternatives to medication.
© Reluctantly agree to try hypnotherapy and return for a review in three weeks.

CANDIDATE CARD NO. 3 MEDICINE

SETTING Medical Centre

DOCTOR Your patient is a 40-year-old long-term smoker with a history of epilepsy since
childhood. He/she has been trying to quit smoking with no other aids but has been
unsuccessful. The patient has come to request that you prescribe him/her Zyban
(bupropion), an anti-smoking medication.

TASK © Enquire about the patient's smoking history and attempts to quit.

* Explain that Zyban is not suitable for epileptics because the drug can cause fits.

e Explain that Zyban interferes with the effectiveness of epileptic treatment and
that fits can be quite severe (e.g., require hospitalisation, etc.).

* Politely refuse to prescribe Zyban and explain that there are other quitting
methods available.

¢ Suggest other methods (e.g., nicotine lozenges, patches, etc.) including
hypnotherapy (hypnosis to help quit smoking) and recommend that the patient
choose a hypnotherapist with a good success rate.

¢ Persuade the patient to retum for a review in three weeks.

SETTING -: ‘ Suburban Medical Clinic

PATIENT You are a 52-year-old smoker. Over the last six months, you have experienced
occasions of breathlessness and chest pain on exertion. You are worried about the
pain because your father died of a heart attack at 53.

TASK e . heavy, central, discomfort that sometimes occurs
when walking your dog up a steep | hill close to your house, and seems to be
happening more often. The’pain seitles after a few minutes of rest.

* State that you are worried about having a heart attack.

¢ Seek the doctor's advice on doing physical activities.

¢ Get upset when the doctor advises you to stop smoking. You understand why it
. is important but you have failed many times before to stop smoking.

CANDIDATE CARD NO. 4 : MEDICINE
SETTING Suburban Medical Clinic
DOCTOR Your patient is a 52-year-old smoker. Over the last six months, hé/she’has

experienced occasions of breathlessness and chest pain on exertion. You diagnose
angina after asking about the type of pain.

TASK " © Ask the patient to: describe 'the pain.

* Explain your diagnosis: angina (reduced blood/oxygen supply to the heart) and
reassure the patient that the condition can be effectively managed.

* Explain the need to assess other risk factors — fasting glucose, cholesterol, BP —
and recommend an immediate assessment by a cardiologist.

* Caution against strenuous exercise.

* Stress the importance of smoking cessation. Offer to discuss ways of helping the
patient to quit smoking.

© Cambridge Boxhill Language Assessment * SEPTEMBER 2015
